newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas Stock Exchange had boom '96, sees repeat.
newsitem.headline: Caracas Stock Exchange had boom '96, sees repeat.

text.p: The Caracas Stock Exchange, the world's best performing market in 1996, rose 101.5 percent in dollar terms last year, Alejandro Salcedo, president of the exchange said Tuesday.
He told a news conference that in bolivar terms the rise was 321.3 percent with the leading 19-share index yield up 231.3 percent, "the highest rate in Latin America."
Among factors accounting for the boom, Salcedo singled out "the big development of mutual funds, which at the end of the year represented assets over 60 billion bolivars" ($126 million).
Traded volume totalled a record 1.49 trillion bolivars ($3.91 billion), up 77 percent on 1995. Foreign investment jumped 82 percent to reach $835.6 million.

Salcedo saw an even brighter future for the Caracas bolsa in 1997. "The macroeconomic conditions that are beginning to be felt could create a favorable environment for the development and deepening of our capital markets."
He mentioned upcoming planned privatizations, including companies from state-owned mining conglomerate Corporacion Venezolana de Guayana (CVG).
